  "text": "By morning the tide had gone out farther than Tobias remembered. The boats rested crookedly in the harbour mud. At the church he found sand on the step and brushed it away with his boot before going in.

He sat in the last pew. There was no service that day.

From there he could see the upper part of Maren's house through the plain glass beside the door. The front window was dark. Nothing moved on the path.

At nine he went up with the loaf he had bought for her on Monday. He had forgotten to bring it then. The paper had softened where his hand held it.

All eleven posts stood straight.

The door was shut. He knocked once, waited, and tried the latch. It lifted easily.

The lamp stood on the sill, unlit. Her father's rug lay square with the boards. Tobias put the loaf on the table and kept his coat on.

There was sand in one of her shoes beside the hearth. He picked it up, meaning to empty it outside, then set it down again.

He left by the front door and pulled it shut until the latch caught.

At the gate he heard a small sound from the house. Paper settling, perhaps. The loaf had been warm when he bought it, two days ago.

He went back as far as the porch.

Through the window he could see the table. The loaf was still where he had left it.

He waited for her to come and put it away.",
